root_cause.text: The IDLETIMER target lacks a cross-revision compatibility check when reusing an existing timer by label, so revision 0 rules incorrectly call mod_timer() on the uninitialized timer_list field of a timer that was created with alarm semantics by revision 1.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that "If the label was created first by revision 1 with XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM, the object uses alarm timer semantics and timer->timer is never initialized. Reusing that object from revision 0 causes mod_timer() on an uninitialized timer_list." The patch adds a check: `if (info->timer->timer_type & XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM)` and returns -EINVAL to prevent this reuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent adding a rule with the same label but a different timer type (alarm vs. non-alarm) to avoid inconsistent timer behavior.
intent_record.what: Added a check in idletimer_tg_checkentry that rejects rule addition if an existing timer with the same label has the XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM flag set.
intent_record.how: When adding a new rule with a label already in use, the code now verifies that the existing timer's type does not include XT_IDLETIMER_ALARM. If it does, the function returns -EINVAL and prevents the rule from being added.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent adding a rule with the same label but a different timer type (alarm vs. non-alarm) to avoid inconsistent timer behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The group adds a check to prevent mixing alarm and non-alarm timer types for the same label, which directly addresses the vulnerability where a revision 0 rule incorrectly reuses a timer created with alarm semantics by revision 1.

candidates.rationale: Directly calls mod_timer() on the timer_list field of a timer that may have been created with alarm semantics (revision 1), where the timer_list is uninitialized. The missing cross-revision compatibility check allows this unsafe operation.

Reuses an existing timer by label without verifying that the timer was created under the same revision. This allows a revision 0 rule to obtain a revision 1 (alarm) timer, leading to the subsequent unsafe mod_timer call.
Increments the reference count on a timer that may be from a different revision, enabling shared use without a compatibility check, which sets the stage for the vulnerable mod_timer call.

bic_trace_step.reason: The idletimer_tg_checkentry function (lines ~180-210) reuses an existing timer by label (via __idletimer_tg_find_by_label) and unconditionally calls mod_timer() on it, without any check for the timer's revision (e.g., whether it was created with alarm semantics). This missing cross-revision compatibility check is the root cause: later, when revision 1 adds alarm timers, revision 0 rules will call mod_timer() on an uninitialized timer_list field. The code also lacks any revision field or handling, so the vulnerability is present from this initial commit.
